modern-eloquence-vol-iii-after-dinner-sp:
Volume Three completes the after-dinner speeches in Thomas B. Reed's Modern Eloquence. Geo. L. Shuman and Company published it at Chicago, with copyright in 1903. Reed's associate editors were again Justin McCarthy, Rossiter Johnson, and Albert Ellery Bergh. This volume runs from speakers P through Z.

Its frontispiece is a photogravure of Priscilla and John Alden, the Puritan courtship New England orators loved to cite. A committee of selection chose the contents from the era's banquet circuit. Together the volumes form a library of occasional addresses, lectures, and toasts. They preserve how public men entertained and persuaded after dinner.
